arxiv-2203-17273.title: FindIt: Generalized Localization with Natural Language Queries
arxiv-2203-17273.creator: Weicheng Kuo, Fred Bertsch, Wei Li, AJ Piergiovanni, Mohammad Saffar, Anelia Angelova
arxiv-2203-17273.description: Abstract We propose FindIt, a simple and versatile framework that unifies a variety of visual grounding and localization tasks including referring expression comprehension, text-based localization, and object detection. Key to our architecture is an efficient multi-scale fusion module that unifies the disparate localization requirements across the tasks.

arxiv-2207-02598.title: Predicting is not Understanding: Recognizing and Addressing Underspecification in Machine Learning
arxiv-2207-02598.creator: Damien Teney, Maxime Peyrard, Ehsan Abbasnejad
arxiv-2207-02598.description: Abstract Machine learning (ML) models are typically optimized for their accuracy on a given dataset. However, this predictive criterion rarely captures all desirable properties of a model, in particular how well it matches a domain expert’s understanding of a task.

arxiv-2405-20284.title: Fock’s dimer model on the Aztec diamond
arxiv-2405-20284.creator: Cédric Boutillier, Béatrice de Tilière
arxiv-2405-20284.description: Abstract We consider the dimer model on the Aztec diamond with Fock’s weights, which is gauge equivalent to the model with any choice of positive weight function. We prove an explicit, compact formula for the inverse Kasteleyn matrix, thus extending numerous results in the case of periodic graphs.

arxiv-2502-07645.title: From Action Labels to Sets: Rethinking Action Supervision for Imitation Learning from Corrective Feedback
arxiv-2502-07645.creator: Zhaoting Li, Rodrigo Pérez-Dattari, Robert Babuska, Cosimo Della Santina and Jens Kober
arxiv-2502-07645.description: Abstract Behavior cloning (BC) optimizes policies by treating human demonstrations as pointwise action labels. While effective with accurate action labels, this formulation is brittle in practice: when human-provided actions are imperfect, treating each label as an exact target can steer the policy away from the underlying desired behavior, particularly when expressive models are used (e.g., energy-based models).

arxiv-2511-17855.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jordan Abi Nader, David Lee, Nathaniel Dennler, Andreea Bobu. Robots must learn from both what people do and what they say, but either modality alone is often incomplete: physical corrections are grounded but ambiguous in intent, while language expresses high-level goals but lacks physical grounding. We introduce QuickLAP : Quick Language–Action Preference learning , a Bayesian framework that fuses physical and language feedback to infer reward functions in real time.

pmc-10577220.creator: Junxiong Lu, Mingzhen Chen, Guansheng He, Binwei Chen, Ruolun Wang
pmc-10577220.description: Objective: Postoperative pain management is an important part of surgical pharmacy. Postoperative acute pain services in China are in their initial stages. This survey aimed to investigate the attitudes, involvement, and knowledge of clinical pharmacists in China regarding postoperative acute pain services.

pmc-11565125.title: Evaluating the mitochondrial structure and gene expression profile of regenerated liver tissues in mice after 85% partial hepatectomy
pmc-11565125.creator: Yongquan Shi, Yu Lei, Yanping Zhao, Shuaishuai Zhang, Hongxin Xu, Li Huo, Wei Liu, Qinlong Liu
pmc-11565125.description: BackgroundPartial hepatectomy (PH) is the primary method used for treating liver injury and transplantation. The regeneration process after hepatectomy requires an adequate energy supply, and mitochondria serve as the primary source of energy. Alterations in genes related to the respiratory chain complex may impact the liver regeneration process.

pmc-12406386.title: Uncovering the genetic landscape of soybean accessions from Kazakhstan in comparison with global germplasm using whole genome resequencing
pmc-12406386.creator: Alibek Zatybekov, Yuliya Genievskaya, Chao Fang, Saule Abugalieva, Yerlan Turuspekov
pmc-12406386.description: BackgroundSoybean (Glycine max) is a globally important crop, yet its genetic diversity remains underutilized in breeding programs, particularly in emerging production regions such as Kazakhstan. As Kazakhstan expands its soybean cultivation, a detailed understanding of the genetic diversity and population structure of both local and international germplasm is critical for developing regionally adapted cultivars.

pmc-12559617.title: To Choose or Not to Choose: Patients with Chest Pain Often Do Not Choose to Triage for Chest Pain During Online Self-Triage
pmc-12559617.creator: Jennifer L. Pecina, Elizabeth N. Curry, Nathaniel E. Miller, Matthew C. Thompson, Frederick North
pmc-12559617.description: Background:Patients performing self-triage for chest pain need to pick an algorithm which includes questions pertinent to chest pain to triage accurately.Objective:Our study reviews patient self-triage choices and outcomes for patients who completed an online self-triage encounter before being triaged by a nurse for chest pain.

pmc-12698044.title: Commentary: Beneficial non-specific effects of measles vaccine: Fact or fiction?
pmc-12698044.creator: Peter Aaby, Sebastian Nielsen, Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer, Cesario Martins, Christine S Benn
pmc-12698044.description: A PLOS One review has claimed that randomized controlled trials (RCTs) show no beneficial nonspecific effects (NSEs) of measles vaccine (MV). Since this claim contradicts previous meta-analyses, we examined the contradictory views. RCTs of MV in low-income countries have mainly tested standard-titer-measles vaccine (STMV) vs high-titer-measles-vaccine (HTMV) (1980–90s) and two-dose vs one-dose of STMV (2000–10s).

pmc-12763926.title: Occurrence of benzodiazepines and nonbenzodiazepines usage among newly-onset of peritoneal dialysis versus hemodialysis patients
pmc-12763926.creator: Wen-Teng Lee, Mingchih Chen, Yu-Wei Fang, Wei-Shan Chang, Kai-Yuan Hsiao, Ben-Chang Shia, Hung-Hsiang Liou, Ming-Hsien Tsai
pmc-12763926.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe use of central nervous system depressants, including benzodiazepines (BZDs) and nonbenzodiazepine hypnotics (Z-drugs), is increasingly observed in chronic dialysis patients. Hemodialysis (HD) and peritoneal dialysis (PD) patients differ in physiological stress and neuropsychiatric profiles, yet both groups are exposed to medications such as BZDs and Z-drugs, whose adverse effects including sedation, cognitive impairment, and increased mortality, may further compound the psychological vulnerability and survival risks inherent to these dialysis populations.

pmc-13047216.title: Neutralizing autoantibodies against interferon alpha in systemic lupus erythematosus: Prevalence, age of onset, and clinical associations
pmc-13047216.creator: Elsa Grenmyr, Birgitta Gullstrand, Andreas Jern, Niklas Björklund, Robin Kahn, Fredrik Kahn, Petrus Linge, Andreas Jönsen, Anders A Bengtsson
pmc-13047216.description: ObjectiveType I interferons (IFN) drive systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) pathogenesis. Some patients develop neutralizing IFN autoantibodies (anti-IFN ab), which theoretically could modify disease activity. We aimed to determine the prevalence of anti-IFN ab in patients with SLE, identify the age and when during the disease course of anti-IFN ab emerge, and assess their association with organ damage.

pmc-13077871.title: The relative cost-effectiveness of atraumatic needles compared to conventional needles in diagnostic lumbar punctures
pmc-13077871.creator: James Evans, Julia Lowin, Pippa Anderson
pmc-13077871.description: IntroductionClinical evidence indicates that atraumatic needles (ATNs) versus conventional needles (CNs) reduce diagnostic lumbar puncture (DLP) complications. Despite this, the use of CNs in DLP remains widespread. This analysis estimates the cost-effectiveness of ATNs versus CNs in DLP.MethodsWe constructed a model mapping DLP patient pathways and complications (limited to PDPH events and PDPH-related hospitalisations/epidural blood patches (EBP)).

Geographic barriers create fluctuating supply, contributing to high levels of poly-drug use and increased overdose risk. pmc-13404459.title: Population Structure and Local Adaptation of Acrossocheilus yunnanensis in the Headwaters of the Chishui River
pmc-13404459.creator: Ji Huang, Xianjie Huang, Qun Lu, Jianhu Liu, Shuang Li, Mengru Wang, Chunlin Zhang
pmc-13404459.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Simple SummaryAcrossocheilus yunnanensis plays an important ecological role in the headwaters of the Chishui River; however, research on its genetic structure and environmental adaptation in this region remains inadequate. Therefore, whole-genome resequencing was applied to analyze the genetic structure of seven geographic populations in this area, and runs of homozygosity (ROH) were further utilized to calculate FROH for evaluating the genomic health of each population.
